issues.legal_issue: A leaseholder's entitlement to hereditary-tenant status depends on whether the lease was made for the leaseholder's personal cultivation and not for other purposes.
material_facts: The landholders granted leases that allowed the leaseholders to remain in possession either themselves or through temporary tenants, and to recover government revenue.
The later lease also allowed the leaseholders to appoint temporary tenants.
The lower consolidation authority denied the leaseholders hereditary-tenant status, and the High Court dismissed their challenge.
issues.conclusion: The leases were not made solely for the leaseholders' personal cultivation because their terms contemplated other purposes. The leaseholders therefore did not qualify as hereditary tenants under Section 12. The appeal was allowed, the High Court and revisional orders were set aside, and the Settlement Officer's order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 requires that the claimant be in possession on 1 May 1950, hold possession under a theka, and hold it under a theka made with a view to personal cultivation by that thekedar, rather than for other purposes. The statute's object is to secure land for the tiller. Under Section 13(2)(a), a thekedar appointed to collect rent from other tenants who is merely allowed to cultivate the lessor's land incidentally is an assami. Balu Noorul Hassan Khan (Dead) by LRs v. Ram Prasad Singh was followed; Rani Dullaiya v. Ganga Prasad was overruled insofar as it treated a lease for other purposes as sufficient when it also provided for personal cultivation.

predicates.thekedar_status_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether persons holding land under a theka qualify for hereditary-tenant status.
predicates.lease_authorized_other_purposes: The lease terms permitted the land to be held or used for purposes other than the leaseholder's personal cultivation, such as through temporary tenants.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns hereditary-tenant status under a theka and the lease permits purposes other than the leaseholder's personal cultivation, the leaseholders do not acquire hereditary-tenant status.
